data.title: REE Automotive Secures $4 Million Equity Commitment as It Advances Court‑Supervised Restructuring
data.description:
REE Automotive ( (REEAF) ) has provided an update.

On October 19, 2026, REE Automotive entered into an equity commitment letter with investors Kukac LLC and Elljay Limited for a $4 million equity injection to provide working capital during a proposed debt restructuring under Israel’s Insolvency and Economic Rehabilitation Law. The funds are ring-fenced from creditor distributions, while up to $3 million of existing cash and future revenues would be set aside for eligible creditors and proceeding costs, and creditors could receive up to an additional $3 million contingent on a qualifying exit transaction by September 30, 2029.

The restructuring plan calls for cancelling all existing equity, converting certain debts, including loans from CEO Daniel Barel and CTO Ahishay Sardes and qualifying convertible notes, into new share classes, and leaving the post‑restructuring ownership split at 60% for the new investors, 29% for Barel and Sardes combined, and 11% for convertible noteholders. REE has moved swiftly in Israeli court, winning authorization on October 20, 2026, to convene creditor meetings on October 25, with objections due October 27 and a potential hearing on October 28, but the transaction remains subject to creditor and court approval, satisfaction of conditions before a November 15, 2026 closing deadline, and the company’s planned delisting from Nasdaq to become a private entity, all of which carry significant uncertainty for existing shareholders and creditors.

data.title: T3 Defense Regains Nasdaq Equity Compliance After Warrant Exercises
data.description:
T3 Defense ( (DFNS) ) has provided an announcement.

T3 Defense Inc. disclosed that it had fallen out of compliance with Nasdaq’s $10 million minimum stockholders’ equity requirement after its June 30, 2026 Form 10-Q showed equity had swung from approximately $42.5 million at March 31, 2026 to a deficit of about $19.7 million, largely due to non-cash warrant liability remeasurement tied to a February 24, 2026 private placement. By September 30, 2026, holders had exercised roughly 96% of the outstanding warrants, eliminating most of the warrant liability and lifting pro forma stockholders’ equity to about $99.9 million, leading management to assert that the company has regained compliance while awaiting Nasdaq’s formal determination and facing ongoing monitoring and potential delisting risk if future reports fail to demonstrate continued compliance.

The company’s equity deterioration stemmed from the accounting treatment of its common warrants as liability-classified instruments, which caused their carrying amount to rise from approximately $24.5 million at December 31, 2025 to about $124.4 million at June 30, 2026 and pushed equity negative despite underlying operations. With the warrant exercises largely completed and the liability reduced to a de minimis residual, T3 Defense has asked Nasdaq to resolve the previously disclosed deficiency and confirm its continued listing, though the outcome and any conditions or monitoring periods remain uncertain for shareholders and other stakeholders.

data.title: Ionis Advances IgA Nephropathy Program With Positive Phase 3
data.description:
The latest update is out from Ionis Pharmaceuticals ( (IONS) ).

On October 23, 2026, Ionis’ partner Roche reported late‑breaking Phase 3 data from the ongoing IMAgINATION trial in adults with primary IgA nephropathy, showing investigational antisense therapy sefaxersen cut proteinuria by a statistically significant and clinically meaningful 43.1% versus placebo at 37 weeks, with consistent effects across prespecified subgroups. The drug, a once‑monthly subcutaneous injection targeting complement factor B, was well tolerated and also improved hematuria resolution, underscoring its potential to address major unmet needs in a chronic kidney disease that frequently progresses to end‑stage renal failure and reinforcing Ionis’ strategic position in RNA‑based therapeutics through its Roche licensing deal.

The IMAgINATION study, which enrolled 459 high‑risk IgAN patients, will remain blinded to assess longer‑term kidney function over 105 weeks, while Roche engages health authorities on the data. For Ionis, positive Phase 3 results in a first‑in‑class RNA‑targeted therapy for IgAN highlight the commercial and clinical upside of its antisense platform, with future regulatory and sales milestones and tiered royalties on potential sefaxersen sales offering meaningful value for investors and signaling competitive pressure in the emerging IgAN treatment market.

data.title: Bolt Biotherapeutics Completes Prana Merger, Refocuses Pipeline
data.description:
Bolt Biotherapeutics ( (BOLT) ) has issued an announcement.

On October 23, 2026, Bolt Biotherapeutics completed a sign‑and‑close reverse merger to acquire Prana Therapies in a stock‑for‑stock transaction, issuing common shares and Series D non‑voting convertible preferred stock that will convert into common stock following shareholder approval. The deal shifts Bolt’s strategic focus to Prana’s INSPIRE platform and PRA‑216, a Phase 2 IL‑4Rα/TSLP bispecific antibody for major inflammatory indications, while bringing Prana’s founder Sheila Gujrathi onto Bolt’s board and executive team.

Concurrent with the acquisition, Bolt arranged a $120 million private placement, with the potential for an additional $60 million upon exercise of warrants, selling Series D preferred shares to accredited healthcare investors in an unregistered PIPE expected to fund operations into 2028. The company also formalized the rights and limitations of its new Series D preferred stock, including dividend parity with common shares, restricted voting powers, conversion mechanics, and ownership caps designed to manage control and dilution as Bolt’s shareholder base shifts toward Prana holders and PIPE investors.
